title: Traffic sculpting experiments and rollback log (personal lab notes)
content:
Context:
- Quick personal notes from running a few small-scale traffic-sculpting experiments on the 2025-11 canary. Trying non-uniform traffic splits and time-windowed rampups to reduce blast radius while keeping request latency under 250ms p50.
- Goal: find pragmatic rules we can bank into the micro-rollout helper script and include in the preflight checklist. This is not policy doc, just my lab record.

High-level hypothesis:
- Small, directional traffic probes that vary by client cohort (by API key tag) + gradual per-region step-ups produce faster signal for bad regressions than single global percent ramps.
- Rate-slicing (throttling a portion of traffic to a slower/cheaper variant) reduces cost exposure and yields a clearer error surface for model regressions.

Experiment matrix (summary):
- A: Global 1% -> 5% -> 25% (linear) over 90m (control)
- B: Cohort probe: 0.5% of high-traffic API keys (10 keys) constant for 60m, then expand to additional 1% groups
- C: Region-first: region-us-west 5% -> 15% over 45m, other regions held at 0% for 2h
- D: Rate-slice: route 10% of traffic to quantized-variant vQ and 90% to baseline; observe error/quality divergence

Quick notes / outcomes (raw):
- A: Good for overall stability metrics, but noisy for small regressions; p95 distance hides early model quality drift.
- B: Fastest detection for semantic-quality issues (bleeding hallucinations). Because cohort included customers with longer prompts, regression surfaced at ~18m.
- C: Good for catching infra/cold-start issues specific to region, but delayed signal for cross-region model regressions.
- D: Excellent for cost-probing and understanding quantization artifacts; watch for tail latency on vQ under high seq-len.

Metrics to capture (minimum pass for future runs):
- Per-cohort: request count, error rate (5xx/4xx), mean/max latency, rejection-rate, model-quality score (via eval hooks)
- Delta metrics: relative quality delta vs baseline at 15m, 30m, 60m
- Safety sentinels: spike in hallucination tags from heuristic, token-injection alarms, prompt-truncation increases

Actionable rollout heuristics I want to try next (to add to script):
1) Cohort-first probes (preferred): select 3 low-latency/high-coverage API keys as canary cohorts. Start at 0.5% user traffic but keep them sticky for 45–90m.
2) If cohort shows >1.5x baseline error OR quality delta > 5% on our eval metric at 30m -> STOP and auto-pin fallback variant (pin by model hash + route).
3) If cohort shows minor diffs (quality delta 1–5%) -> expand to second cohort and enable rate-slice 10% to the variant while routing rest to baseline for 60m.
4) For region-sensitive rollouts, do region-first with lower step size (5% steps) and a 2x monitoring window per step.

Quick rollback checklist (manual steps, condensed):
- When to roll back: sustained error above threshold OR bad-quality regression that affects top 3 intents for a customer cohort.
- Immediate steps:
  - 1) Notify #deploys and on-call SRE (pager) with short TL;DR + link to traces and dashboard.
  - 2) Pin route to previous model version via console API: POST /routes/<route>/pin {model: "model@sha:abcd1234"} OR use infra helper script: ./tools/pin-route --route X --model abcd1234
  - 3) If pin not feasible (deploy pipeline locked), flip traffic to warm fallback region that still runs baseline cluster.
  - 4) Activate emergency rate-limiter: set per-route token bucket to 50% of normal throughput to reduce overload and queue growth.
  - 5) Run lightweight RS replay on 1k recent failing requests to compare behavior pinned vs current variant.
  - 6) Create incident note in Confluence with tags and link to recording.

Edge cases / gotchas observed:
- Pin latency: pin operations take ~45–90s to reach all proxies in a region. During that time error spikes can continue; be ready to use rate-limits.
- Model hash mismatch: ensure we use immutable model artifact ids; avoid human-friendly labels for pinning.
- Sticky clients: some SDKs stick to older connection pools; a full client restart/cookie TTL may be required to observe pinned traffic quickly. Note to ask SDK team to add an explicit header to force rebind on model-change.

Simulated rollback run (notes):
- Simulated fault injected via chaos script (delay 120ms per token) at 03:20 UTC; cohort-first probe detected p50 latency +40% at 03:37 (within 17m).
- Took actions: notified, pinned to model@sha:ef90c1, set token-bucket to 50% at 03:45, replayed 1k requests.
- Post-pin: errors reduced to baseline in ~6 minutes; traffic normalized by 04:05.
- Learnings: for token-delay faults, pinning + rate-limit is faster recovery than full rollback in 80% of runs.

To-do / follow-ups (short):
- Convert cohort-selection heuristics into small helper CLI (input: api-key list, sample size, traffic percent).
- Add a preflight probe that can run a mini-eval on a 50-sample prompt set and surface quality delta in the UI.
- Align with SDK team about header to force client rebind on model pin (ticket: INF-2240).
- Draft a short page for product on how cohort probing works; keep it high-level.

Open questions (unresolved):
- What should the default quality-delta threshold be for semantic regressions? 3% vs 5%? Need to correlate with user-facing incidents from past six months.
- Should we treat region-only regressions as lower priority for rollback vs model-quality regressions? My intuition: treat them the same if user-facing latency crosses SLO.
- How to better synthesize small-sample eval deltas into a single decision score that non-ML reviewers can understand?

Notes to self (short):
- Keep experiment logs attached to the ticket (INF-2145) and include sample requests/responses (redact private prompts).
- When running cohort probes, try to pick API keys that represent a range of seq-lens. That surfaced the quantization issue in run D.
- If we add automated pin triggers, build a manual-confirm fallback and an escalation chain — never let automation fully flood without human on-call during initial rollout.

End of notes.

-- Taylor
